# No External Assets

**Decision:** every visual and audio asset in [[stickfps]] must be generated in code. No model files,
no texture files, no audio files, no font files. Stated as a hard filter on the design itself, not as
a technique:

> "**If a design needs an asset, it must be procedurally generatable in code, or it's out.**"
> — browser_game_stickfps/DESIGN_PROMPT.md, 2026-07-25

## What that means concretely

- **Geometry** — the entire arena from box, plane and cylinder primitives in a 576-line
  `Environment.tsx`; stickmen generated procedurally. See [[three-js]].
- **Audio** — all SFX synthesised with the Web Audio API in a 300-line `sounds.ts`. Zero audio files.
- **Textures** — inline SVG data URIs.
- **Type** — system UI fonts.

## Why it holds up

It removes an entire class of work that a solo browser project cannot afford: sourcing, licensing,
optimising, hosting and cache-busting binary assets. There is no asset pipeline, no CDN, no
attribution ledger, and no licence question about anything shipped.

It also makes the visual identity **reviewable**. Art becomes code that diffs, and a design change is
an edit rather than a re-export from a tool the repo does not contain. When the film-noir grayscale
identity was retired for full colour ([[superseded-in-place-documentation]]), the change was a code
change — with no assets to re-author, reversing a whole art direction stayed cheap.

## What it costs

The art ceiling is set by what primitives can express, and everything renders from setup code rather
than from optimised buffers. The bundle is still ~1.4 MB, so this bought no size win — the weight is
[[react-three-fiber]] and its dependencies, not content. Some visual ideas are simply unavailable.

## Where it sits in the wider habit

[[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] is contradicted at the toolchain level here — [[stickfps]] has
twelve runtime dependencies and two build pipelines ([[vite]]). But the same instinct reappears one
layer down as an absolute rule: **refuse the asset pipeline wherever code can replace it.** The
coursework repositories refuse the build step; this one accepts the build step and refuses the
content.

That is the more precise statement of the pattern across the source set: the thing being avoided is a
*fetched, opaque, unversioned input*, not tooling as such.
